transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... well, ever since I got that county safety award last month, things have been weird. You know, they give you this little plaque with the brass lettering—mine actually had a scratch on the 'T' in transportation, but I didn't say anything because the guy who hands them out, Frank, he's always complaining about his arthritis. Anyway, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports. Asking all these pointed budget questions, like they're trying to make me look crooked or something. Which is funny, because I've always been a stickler for the budget. I even buy my own pens, the blue gel ones, because the cheap ballpoints they supply just smear on the carbon copies. But even when my supervisor says it's just a 'normal review,' I can tell. I can just tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. It's like they're all in on it.
When you say people are twisting your reports and there's a coordinated effort against you—do you have any doubt about whether this is actually happening, or are you completely certain it's real?

Doubt? No, no doubt at all. I'm completely certain. You just have to look at the budget questions they're asking, they're so pointed. Like they want to catch me slipping up and make me look crooked. Which is ridiculous because I check everything twice. 

Just like when I check the brake lines on the county buses. You know, they switched to a new supplier for the brake pads last year, and they smell terrible when they get hot. Like burning hair or something. I told the fleet manager about it, but he just brushed me off. He's always eating those stale powdered donuts in his office anyway, getting white dust all over the keyboards. It's impossible to type on his computer without getting it on your sleeves. 

But yeah, my supervisor tries to play it off. He tells me, "It's just a normal review." But I know what a normal review looks like, I've been doing this for years. I can tell they're twisting my reports. Ever since I got that safety award, it's been a coordinated effort against me. I'm sure of it.

When you say people are twisting your reports and asking pointed budget questions to discredit you—is this something that could actually happen in the real world, or does it involve something impossible or that violates the laws of nature?

Laws of nature? I... I'm not really sure what you mean by that. I mean, of course it happens in the real world, it's just people messing with my paperwork. It's just regular office politics, really. 

And office politics are very real. It's like when they decided to rearrange the breakroom downstairs last month. They moved the microwave right next to the refrigerator, which makes absolutely no sense because the microwave door swings the wrong way now. You have to lean awkwardly over the recycling bin just to get your food out. I was heating up some leftover lasagna on Tuesday—my sister makes it with this spicy sausage she gets from the Italian butcher over on 4th street. The guy who runs that place has a glass eye, and he always gives you an extra quarter pound of prosciutto if you go in right before they close, around 5:30. Best deli meats in the whole county, honestly. 

But yeah, I don't know about anything impossible or violating nature or whatever. It's just them trying to catch me slipping up on the budget.

You mentioned people at work twisting your reports and asking pointed questions about the budget. When you think about how they're doing this—is it something that uses normal means like changing documents or talking to others, or does it involve something strange or unusual like reading your mind, or controlling what you do?

No, no mind reading or anything crazy like that. They're just doing it the normal way—changing numbers on the spreadsheets before they go to the director, whispering in the halls when I walk by. Just regular underhanded stuff. 

Speaking of the halls, though, they finally fixed that flickering fluorescent light on the second floor near the stairwell. It was driving me crazy. It had this high-pitched hum, you know? Like a mosquito right by your ear. I told maintenance about it three times, but they're always so backed up. The guy who usually changes the bulbs, Steve, he's been out on medical leave because he slipped on some ice in his driveway and twisted his ankle. His wife actually makes these incredible snickerdoodle cookies—she brought a whole tin of them in for the holiday party last year. They had just the right amount of cinnamon. I tried to get the recipe from her, but she said it was a family secret that her grandmother brought over from Germany. Or maybe it was Austria? I can't remember. 

But yeah, they're not controlling my thoughts or anything. They're just messing with the paperwork to make me look bad.

When you think about what's happening at work—the people twisting your reports, the pointed budget questions, all of it—do you see this as one main thing they're doing to you, or are there several completely different things going on that aren't really connected to each other?

Well, it's... it's all one big thing. It's all connected. The reports, the budget questions, the whispering. It's all part of the same effort to get me out of there. 

Just like how everything is connected with the bus routes. You change one stop on the 42 line, and suddenly the 15 is running late because of the transfer traffic at the transit center. The transit center downtown, you know, the one with the big glass dome? They have to wash that glass every two weeks because of the pigeons. There's this guy, Gary, who does the washing. He uses this special squeegee on a really long pole. He was telling me the other day about how his daughter just started playing the cello. She's only eight, but apparently she's a prodigy or something. She's playing Vivaldi already. I don't know much about classical music, but I prefer country anyway. There's a station I listen to on my drive in, 98.5, and they do this segment every morning where they call someone and play a prank on them. It's pretty funny. 

But yeah, the stuff at work, it's all just one big coordinated effort against me. It's not random.

You mentioned people at work changing numbers on spreadsheets and whispering in the halls. If someone wanted to do these things—change your reports and spread rumors about you—is that something that's actually possible for people to do in the real world, or does it require something that couldn't really happen?

I mean, yeah, of course it's possible. Anyone can open an Excel file and change a number, or talk behind someone's back. It's totally real-world stuff, nothing impossible about it. 

Just like it's totally possible for the city to finally fix the potholes on Elm Street. Have you driven down there lately? They finally filled that massive crater right near the intersection with Maple. I swear, that thing was going to swallow my car whole one of these days. My buddy Dave—he drives a tow truck—he said he pulled three cars out of that exact spot last winter when it rained and filled up like a kiddie pool. Dave's a good guy, he actually helped me install a new alternator in my truck last weekend. We spent like four hours in his garage. His garage is amazing, by the way, he's got this vintage neon Budweiser sign that he found at a garage sale for like ten bucks. Can you believe that? Ten bucks for real neon. He's got a whole collection of old license plates covering the back wall, too. 

But yeah, changing spreadsheets and whispering? That's just people being sneaky. Nothing impossible about it at all.

You mentioned that people at work are changing numbers on your spreadsheets and whispering about you to discredit you. Setting aside whether you think it's actually happening to you—is it something that would be physically possible for someone to do, or would it require something that couldn't actually happen in the real world?

I mean, I think I just said that, right? Yeah, it's completely possible. They have access to the shared drives, they walk down the same halls. It doesn't take magic to mess with an Excel file. 

Speaking of computers, though, my laptop at home has been acting up lately. The fan just spins super loud the second I turn it on. It sounds like a jet engine taking off in my living room. I took it to this repair shop over on 4th Street, right next to that new diner that opened up. Have you been there? The diner, I mean. They make this incredible meatloaf sandwich. My buddy Mike and I went there last Tuesday after work. Mike's a dispatcher over at the main yard, and he was telling me how they're bringing in these new hybrid buses next month. Supposedly they're going to cut emissions by like 30 percent, but the mechanics are all complaining because they have to take this special certification course just to touch the engines. The course is down in state capital, so they have to put everyone up in hotels. I remember staying in a hotel there once for a high school field trip, and the ice machine on our floor was broken, so we had to keep going up to the seventh floor... 

But yeah, like I was saying, what they're doing at work is just regular stuff. Sneaky, but totally normal things people do.

You've told me about people at work changing your reports and asking pointed budget questions to discredit you. Is this the main thing that's been troubling you, or are there other separate things happening—maybe outside of work—that you're also concerned about?

Well, no, it's pretty much just the work stuff. That's the main thing. I mean, that's where I spend most of my time anyway, right? At the depot or out on the routes. 

Speaking of the routes, they just redid the schedule for the downtown loop, and let me tell you, it is a complete mess. The new times don't line up with the shift changes at the hospital at all. I was talking to Sarah about it—she's one of the senior drivers, been there for like fifteen years. She drives the early shift on the 12 line. She actually makes these really amazing snickerdoodle cookies and brings them into the breakroom on Fridays. Her secret is she puts a tiny bit of nutmeg in with the cinnamon. I tried making them at home once, but my oven runs hot, so the bottoms got all burnt. I need to get one of those oven thermometers. I saw one at the hardware store when I was picking up some caulk for my bathroom sink. The seal around the faucet was starting to peel, and I didn't want water getting down into the cabinet. The cabinet is this really nice oak finish, it was already there when I rented the place...

But yeah, no, it's just the stuff at work with the reports and the budget. Nothing else really going on outside of that.

You've described people changing numbers on spreadsheets and whispering about you at work. If you think about this very carefully—is there anything about what they're doing that would be impossible according to the laws of physics or nature, or is it all something that people could theoretically do even if it's unfair?

I feel like we're just going in circles here, Doc. I mean, yes, I just said that, didn't I? It's not magic. It's just people being sneaky with computers and talking behind my back. It's completely possible according to physics or whatever. 

Speaking of physics, I was watching this documentary the other night on PBS about black holes and gravity. It's crazy how time actually slows down the closer you get to a black hole. Like, if you fell into one, you'd see the whole future of the universe play out before you died. Or something like that. I don't know, it was late and I was eating a bowl of cereal. Cinnamon Toast Crunch, actually. You know they changed the recipe a few years ago? It doesn't taste the same as when I was a kid. My mom used to buy the giant bags of it from the discount grocery store because my brother and I would go through a box in like two days. My brother lives out in Oregon now, he works for the forestry service. He sends me pictures of these massive redwood trees he hikes past. I told him I'd come visit him this summer, maybe rent a car and drive up the coast. I need to renew my driver's license first, though. The DMV line is always a nightmare, last time I was there I waited three hours and the guy in front of me kept coughing without covering his mouth. 

But yeah, to answer your question again, it's totally possible stuff. Just normal, sneaky stuff. No laws of nature being broken.

When these people at work are asking you budget questions and changing your reports—do you think they're specifically trying to target you because of something about you personally, or are you interpreting their normal work actions as being directed at you in a special way?

Oh, it's definitely personal. It's not me misinterpreting anything. It all started right after I got that county safety award, actually. 

They gave me this really nice glass plaque for it. It's sitting on my desk right now, though I had to move it the other day because the glare from the window hits it right around three o'clock and shines straight into my eyes. The afternoon sun in that office is just brutal. We've been asking facilities to install those pull-down shades for months, but you know how slow the county works. My buddy Dave—he's over in maintenance—said they actually have the shades just sitting in a warehouse across town, they just haven't filed the paperwork to bring them over. That warehouse used to be an old roller rink back in the 90s, actually. I used to go there for birthday parties when I was a kid. We'd get those terrible personal pan pizzas that were basically just grease and cardboard, but man, they tasted amazing after skating for two hours. They always played the loudest pop music, and they had this carpet with the neon shapes on it that glowed under the blacklights...

But anyway, yeah, ever since that safety award, certain people have been twisting my inspection reports and asking all these pointed budget questions. It's like they're specifically trying to make me look crooked. And even when my supervisor says it's just "normal review," I can tell. I'm not stupid. There is a coordinated effort to discredit me, and it's 100 percent directed right at me.

You've mentioned several times that people are changing your spreadsheets and asking budget questions. Let me ask you this directly: Is there anything about what you believe is happening to you—anything at all—that you recognize couldn't actually happen in the real world, or is everything you've described something that really could happen, even if you think it's unfair?

Look, I don't know how many ways I can say it. Yes, it is all completely real. People change numbers on computers. They ask questions to make you look bad. That happens in the real world every single day. 

Speaking of every day, I have to drive past this one house on my inspection route every single day, and they have this massive collection of garden gnomes out front. Like, hundreds of them just covering the entire lawn. It's totally wild. Some of them are painted like sports teams, too. I think I saw a Steelers one yesterday. I used to watch football a lot on Sundays, but the games just have way too many commercials now. You watch three minutes of a game and then it's five minutes of ads for car insurance. 

I actually need to switch my car insurance, now that I think about it. My premium went up because someone backed into my bumper at the grocery store last month and just drove off. I was just inside buying milk and a loaf of bread. They didn't even leave a note, just left a massive dent and some red paint transfer on my silver bumper. I tried rubbing it out with some buffing compound I picked up at AutoZone, but the scratch is pretty deep. The guy at the counter said I'd probably need to get it professionally sanded and repainted, but I don't have the money for that right now. Plus, the AutoZone always smells like burnt rubber and cheap air fresheners, it gives me a headache if I stand in line too long...

But yeah, to answer your question again, it's all just regular, real-world stuff happening to me. Nothing impossible about it.

You've told me about people changing your reports and asking budget questions since you got the safety award. Do you see how all these different things—the changed spreadsheets, the pointed questions, the whispering—are they all part of one clear plan that makes sense when you put it together, or do they feel more like separate things happening that you're connecting?

No, it's definitely all one plan. It all fits together perfectly. The spreadsheets, the questions, the whispering... it's all part of the same coordinated effort to get me fired or, I don't know, discredited or whatever. 

It's kind of like how they build those new highway overpasses, you know? Like, you see them putting up the concrete pillars one month, and then the steel beams go up the next month, and you think, "What is this going to be?" But then they pour the deck and paint the lines, and suddenly it's this massive interchange that connects I-95 to the new bypass. I actually had to inspect the guardrails on that new bypass last week. The contractor they hired used these cheap galvanized bolts instead of the stainless steel ones required in the spec. I wrote it up, of course. You can't mess around with guardrails, especially on those elevated curves. If a semi hits that at 65 miles an hour, those cheap bolts will just sheer right off. 

My buddy Dave—the maintenance guy I mentioned earlier—he drives a semi on the weekends sometimes. He hauls gravel for his uncle's landscaping business. He says the transmission on those things is a nightmare to learn, like 18 gears or something crazy. I don't think I could ever drive one of those. I can barely parallel park my civic, honestly. The steering wheel always gets kind of sticky when it's hot out, I think the power steering fluid is leaking somewhere. I should probably check that this weekend. 

But yeah, it's all one big plan. They're definitely all connected, not just random things happening.

You've described people changing your spreadsheets and asking budget questions to discredit you. Let me ask you something specific: if someone really wanted to do these things to you, would it be something that's actually possible in the real world, or would it require something that couldn't actually happen—like mind control, or messages being sent to you through the TV, or something like that?

Mind control? What? No, no, I'm not talking about anything crazy like that. Nobody is sending me messages through the TV. It's just regular people logging into Excel and messing with my numbers. 

I don't even have regular TV anymore anyway. I cut the cord like three years ago because the cable prices were just getting totally out of hand. They lock you into these promotional rates for twelve months, and then bam, suddenly you're paying a hundred and fifty bucks just to get the local news and the Discovery Channel. 

I used to watch the Discovery Channel all the time, especially during Shark Week. Did you know Great Whites can smell a drop of blood from like three miles away? It's just wild. My buddy Dave went deep-sea fishing down in Florida last summer and said they hooked this massive hammerhead, but it snapped the heavy-duty line right at the boat. He brought back some really good Mahi-Mahi though, and we grilled it on my back patio. 

My grill is actually acting up right now, to be honest. The propane regulator keeps freezing over when I run it on high. I think there's a tiny leak in the hose somewhere. You gotta be really careful with propane, obviously. One spark and the whole deck goes up. I actually need to stop by Home Depot on the way home to get a replacement hose... 

But yeah, I don't know why you're asking about mind control or magic stuff. It's just real people doing real things to my reports. Nothing impossible about it.

You've described people changing your spreadsheets and asking budget questions. I want to be very clear about this: do you believe everything you've told me about what's happening at work—the changed reports, the pointed questions, the coordinated effort—is something that actually could happen in the real world, or is there any part of it that you think is impossible or doesn't make sense according to how the world actually works?

It's all real world stuff. I don't know why we keep going over this. Yes, it's totally possible for someone to log into a shared drive and change a spreadsheet. It happens all the time. Just like it's possible for someone to take my lunch out of the breakroom fridge. 

Actually, that happened last Tuesday. I brought this really good leftover lasagna that my mom made. She makes it with this spicy Italian sausage instead of ground beef, and she puts a layer of spinach in it. It's incredible. Anyway, I put it in the fridge in this blue Tupperware container, and when I went to get it at noon, it was just gone. Someone just took it. I ended up having to get a sandwich from the vending machine, and those things are always soggy. The turkey one I got had this weird, sweet mayonnaise on it. I don't know who puts sweet mayo on turkey. 

I should probably tell my mom to make another batch of that lasagna this weekend. She usually comes over on Sundays to watch my dog, Buster, while I go grocery shopping. Buster is a golden retriever mix, and he sheds like crazy. I have to vacuum my living room rug like three times a week, or it just looks like a fuzzy yellow blanket. I bought one of those expensive Dyson vacuums, the cordless ones? It works great, but the battery only lasts for like twenty minutes on the high setting. I was vacuuming the stairs last night and it just died right in the middle. 

But yeah, the work stuff. It's all real. People messing with spreadsheets and asking questions is just office politics, you know? Nothing impossible about it.

When your supervisor says it's just a 'normal review,' is it possible he's telling you the truth and it really is just a routine review like any other employee might get, or are you completely certain that's impossible and it must be part of the coordinated effort against you?

No, it's impossible that he's telling the truth. I'm completely certain. Even when my supervisor says it's just a normal review, I can tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. It's been happening ever since I got that county safety award. That's exactly when certain people at work started twisting my inspection reports and asking all those pointed budget questions, like they're trying to make me look crooked. 

The award itself was actually this really heavy glass plaque. They handed it to me at the main county building downtown. I almost dropped the thing walking off the stage because my shoes didn't have any grip on the tile floor. I was wearing these cheap dress shoes I got on clearance at Kohl's, and the soles are just completely smooth. Kohl's has a pretty good return policy usually, but I'd already worn them outside so I couldn't take them back. 

My mom loves Kohl's, actually. She gets those Kohl's Cash coupons in the mail all the time and treats it like it's actual money. She used some last week to buy a new toaster because her old one kept burning one side of her bagels. She only eats those cinnamon raisin ones. I can't stand raisins, honestly. They just taste like ruined grapes. When I was a kid, I swallowed a grape whole by accident and choked, and my uncle had to do the Heimlich maneuver on me at a family picnic. He cracked one of my ribs doing it, but I guess it's better than choking to death on a piece of fruit. He's a volunteer firefighter, so he knows all that first aid stuff. They have to do a ton of training for that... 

But yeah, my supervisor is definitely lying to cover up what they're doing.
Is there any possibility at all—even a small one—that your supervisor might actually be telling you the truth when he says it's just a normal review, or are you completely certain that's impossible?

Like I just said, man, zero possibility. I don't know why we're going in circles here. I am completely certain. There is no "small possibility" he's telling the truth. It's a coordinated effort to discredit me, plain and simple. They've been twisting my inspection reports and grilling me on the budget ever since I got that safety award, trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor saying it's a "normal review" is just him playing his part in it to keep me quiet. 

Normal reviews don't look like this. I do normal reviews of county transit vehicles every day, so I know exactly what normal looks like. Like yesterday, I was out at the depot inspecting the undercarriage on one of the articulated buses—you know, the long ones that bend in the middle? Man, the accordion joint on those things gets so much grime stuck in it. I actually found a perfectly good pair of Ray-Bans jammed up in the grease near the hydraulic line. Whoever dropped them must have been pretty mad, those things are like two hundred bucks. 

I used to have a pair of aviators, but I left them on the roof of my car at a Wawa gas station and drove off. Heard this crunching sound on the highway about five miles later. I was driving down Route 9, which is just a complete nightmare for traffic right now because they're repaving the whole stretch near the diner. They've had it down to one lane for three weeks. I don't get why they don't just do the paving at night when nobody is driving. That's what they do in Texas. My buddy lives in Austin and he says they do all their heavy roadwork at like 2 AM. He works at a barbecue place down there. Says the brisket takes fourteen hours to smoke, and you have to use special oak wood or it ruins the flavor... 

But yeah, anyway, no. To answer your question, it's impossible. My supervisor is definitely lying to me.

Besides the people at work changing your reports and trying to discredit you because of the safety award, are there other things happening to you—in other areas of your life, not at work—that you're also concerned or worried about?

No, it's just the work stuff. Outside of that, everything is totally normal. I still get to work on time, I complete all my inspections, take care of myself, and keep up with church. 

Actually, they just replaced all the old wooden pews at my church with these individual padded chairs. I guess the older folks were complaining about their backs. But the chairs are this really ugly maroon color, and the carpet is forest green, so it basically looks like Christmas in there all year round now. My buddy Dave—he usually sits in the back row with me—he actually spilled his coffee on one of the new chairs last Sunday. They set up this little coffee cart in the lobby to try and get people to stick around and talk after the service, but they use that cheap powdered creamer. You know the kind that just clumps up at the top if the coffee isn't boiling hot? It's gross. 

Anyway, Dave works at the Ace Hardware over on 5th Street, and he was telling me that the price of copper wire is just going completely through the roof right now. People are apparently sneaking onto construction sites in the middle of the night just to strip the wiring right out of the walls. It's crazy what people will do for a quick buck. My uncle had his catalytic converter stolen right out of his driveway last year, just sawed it right off...

But yeah, what were we talking about? Oh, my life outside of work. Yeah, it's fine. Like I said, I'm taking care of myself and doing my normal routine. The main problems really only come up when people at the depot bring up those reports or start questioning my spending. That's the only time there's an issue.
Have you noticed anything else strange happening—anything that doesn't quite make sense according to how things normally work—besides what's going on at work with the reports and budget questions?

No, not really. I mean, like I said, it's just the stuff at work. Outside of that, everything makes sense. The world works the way it's supposed to work. Like gravity, you know? You drop something, it falls. 

Actually, speaking of dropping things, I was at the grocery store the other day, and this lady in front of me in the checkout line dropped a whole glass jar of pickles. It just shattered everywhere. The smell was intense—that sharp vinegar smell, you know? It reminded me of when my grandma used to pickle her own cucumbers in the basement. She had these huge ceramic crocks lined up along the wall, and she'd use fresh dill from her garden. Her garden was amazing. She grew these massive beefsteak tomatoes that were so heavy they would snap the vines if you didn't tie them up right. She used pantyhose to tie them up, which sounds weird, but it's soft enough that it doesn't cut into the plant stem. 

My sister tried to start a garden last year, but she lives in this apartment complex where the balcony gets zero sunlight, so all her plants just got spindly and died. She ended up throwing them all in the dumpster out back. That dumpster is always overflowing because the trash company missed their pickup like three weeks in a row. The whole parking lot smells like hot garbage in the summer. 

But no, to answer your question, nothing else strange is happening. Just the work stuff. Everything else is totally normal.

I want to understand something important. When you think about what's happening at work—people changing your spreadsheets and asking those budget questions—is there any small part of you that wonders if maybe you could be misinterpreting things, or are you absolutely certain without any doubt that this is definitely happening exactly as you believe it?

Look, doc, I am absolutely certain. There is no misinterpreting it. Ever since I got that county safety award, they've been twisting my inspection reports and asking all these pointed budget questions. They're trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it's just a normal review, but I can tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. 

It's just like when you're inspecting the brake pads on those older Gillig buses. You know, they use these heavy-duty air brakes, and if the slack adjusters aren't calibrated just right, the whole system pulls to the right when you hit the pedal. I had this one bus last month, bus 409, and the driver kept complaining about a vibration in the steering column. Turns out, the tire pressure was off by like fifteen PSI on the front left. You wouldn't think that would cause a vibration, but it throws the whole alignment out of whack. 

I actually need to get the tires rotated on my truck. It's a Chevy Colorado, and the tread on the back tires is getting pretty bald. I usually take it to this place down on Main Street, but they just raised their prices by like twenty percent. The guy there, Sal, he said it's because of the supply chain issues. Everything is stuck on those cargo ships out in the ocean. I saw a documentary about that on the History Channel. Those ships are massive, they carry like twenty thousand containers at once. Imagine if one of those things sank, all that stuff just sitting at the bottom of the ocean. They find shipwrecks all the time with gold coins and old pottery...

But yeah, I'm not misinterpreting anything. I'm completely certain they're trying to discredit me at work. There's no doubt in my mind.

If I told you that I spoke to your supervisor and he said this really is just a routine review that happens to all employees, and there's no coordinated effort against you—would that change your mind at all, or would you still be certain that something is going on?

No, that wouldn't change my mind one bit. I mean, of course he told you that. Even when my supervisor says it’s just a normal review to my face, I can tell there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me. It's been happening ever since I got that county safety award. They’re twisting my inspection reports and asking these really pointed budget questions because they want to make me look crooked. 

My supervisor actually called me into his office to try and tell me it was routine just last week. His office is right next to the main breakroom, and I swear the walls are paper thin. While he was talking, all I could hear was the microwave beeping. It's this ancient microwave, and the glass turntable is completely busted off its track so it just makes this awful grinding noise when it spins. Someone actually microwaved leftover tilapia in there on Tuesday, and the whole corridor smelled like low tide for three days. You really can't get fish smell out of acoustic ceiling tiles. 

It actually reminded me of when my dad used to take me and my brother ice fishing up on Lake Mille Lacs when we were kids. We'd sit in this tiny wooden shanty for hours. One time, my brother dropped his favorite pair of pliers down the ice hole. They were these really nice needle-nose pliers with the blue rubber grips. He tried to reach down into the freezing water to grab them, but my dad had to yank him back by his snowsuit so he wouldn't fall in. Those snowsuits were so bulky, you could barely put your arms down by your sides. We looked like giant blue marshmallows waddling around on the ice out there. 

But yeah, it doesn't matter what my supervisor told you on the phone. I know exactly what they're doing with those reports and the budget stuff. It's definitely a setup.
